title: Simplicial subdivision of simplices of arbitrary dimension in spaces of constant curvature with bounded quality
summary: In 1942, Freudenthal showed that a simplex in Euclidean space can be subdivided such that the quality (well-shapedness of the simplex, quantified in terms of e.g. fatness) of the simplices in the subdivision is lower bounded. This answered a question of Brouwer. Recently, Brunck discussed the same problem for simplices in two-dimensional spaces of constant curvature and provided a closely related construction. In this paper we generalize Brunck's result to arbitrary dimensional spaces of constant curvature by combining Freudenthal's construction and radial projection. We contrast this…
